summary.text: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Data Science are modern technology domains focused on building intelligent systems, analyzing data, automating processes, and generating business insights. AI enables machines to simulate human intelligence, while ML allows systems to learn from data and improve automatically without explicit programming. Data Science focuses on collecting, processing, analyzing, and visualizing data to support business decisions and predictive analytics. Modern AI platforms such as ChatGPT by OpenAI, Claude by Anthropic, and Gemini by Google are advanced generative AI tools used for content creation, coding assistance, research, automation, customer support, data analysis, and enterprise productivity. These AI systems help businesses improve efficiency, decision-making, and digital transformation initiatives. SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) is an enterprise agile methodology that helps organizations manage large-scale software development and business operations using Agile, Lean, and Scrum practices across multiple teams and departments. These technologies and tools create career opportunities such as AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, Data Analyst, Prompt Engineer, Generative AI Engineer, AI Product Manager, Scrum Master, Agile Coach, and Release Train Engineer. Common technical tools used in these fields include Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, Jupyter Notebook, AWS AI, Azure AI, and Google Cloud AI

title.text: Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Frameworks and Maturity Models

summary.text: I created this LinkedIn group in 2014, having spent 17 years of my life at the time dedicated to the protection of Cybersecurity for public and private sector organizations on both sides of the Atlantic, closely following the development of this critical Cybersecurity Framework for 12 months from 2013 to 2014.  On behalf of my organizations  (HISP Institute and CloudeAssurance), I actively participated in all but 1 of the 5 workshops hosted by NIST in partnership with agencies such as DHS and worked with stakeholders in every industry vertical in the development of this framework. After providing input to the first and second public drafts in 2013 and also expressing my concerns about some of the gaps in the draft documents, now that the final publication has been released, I'm very much committed to not only seeing it's successful implementation, but also committed to ensuring its continual improvement. I decided to rename the group from NIST Cybersecurity Framework to Cybersecurity Frameworks and Maturity Models today 05/05/2022 to include Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) that was published in March 2020 (Version 1.02) and December 2021 (Version 2.0). I decided to rename this group from Cybersecurity Frameworks and Maturity Models to Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Frameworks and Maturity Models today 07/31/2023 to include Artificial Intelligence, that is both an emerging threat and opportunity. This will enable this group to showcase some of the Cybersecurity industry efforts towards making AI Safe and Secure, such as the HISPI's Project Cerebellum, a Think Tank that evolved into a Community of Practice (CoP) for Trusted Artificial Intelligence Model (TAIM): https://projectcerebellum.com I decided to change this group type from private to public today 10/20/2023 since group membership has doubled in the past 1 year and now at 200,000 members. LinkedIn's suggests that making this group public could 1.5x its reach.
